_note: Numbers of the interface, not the sim (design 14 §3; 02 §4). Distances in CSS px, times in ms.

zoom._note: The zoom rail (design 14 §3). Shut it is one 48 px handle in the bottom right, the twin of the Spray chip; a tap opens the rail, a pinch shows it, and a touch on the field puts it away. openMs: how long it stays out after the last touch on it. 0 keeps it out always, the rail as it was.

news._note: The words at the bottom (design 15 A3). speed: CSS px a second at baseWidth; it scales with the real width and never passes maxSpeed. gap: the space between two sentences. queueMax: how many wait before the oldest unshown is dropped. answerMs: how long a reply to the player holds, still, over the crawl. lineMs + perWordMs: how long the Lines style holds one sentence. todayMax: how many the Today list keeps. tapMs: a touch shorter than this opens Today instead of holding the line.

because._note: The Because system (design 14 §4): sparkMs how long the sparkle lingers at the place, tapWorld how near a finger must land (world px), cardMs how long the card is up in all, cardHoldMs how long it is solid before it starts fading, cardGap how far it floats from the spot (CSS px; its size is measured, never assumed), cardHead: the card sits ABOVE the spot, clear of a head this many world px tall (take the key out and it sits beside the spot, as before design 17), whyMs how long a cause icon rides over a head, whyMax how many may ride at once (design 18 F3 and Q41: a busy day 12 put 25 up together, the loudest thing on the screen; the everyday number is 1.1, so six only trims the bursts, and a dropped one is dropped, never queued).

doll._note: The paper doll (design 14 §7 T10): the panel's size in CSS px, how many times over the creature is drawn, and the six slot boxes. The title row over it (Stephen, 25 Sep): the name, or what it is, at nameSize; what a named one is, after it, at kindSize; both a pixel smaller at a time, down to titleMin, until they fit the row. The row lies over the top 16 px of the panel, so the slots start below it.

locator._note: Design 19 A6 (Astra B4, the locator): a tap on the name on a card brings the camera to the one on it (src/ui/find.js). glideMs: how long the camera takes to get there, eased in and out. heartMs: how long the heart that says here it is lasts once the camera is there; beatMs: its one beat, in which it swells by swell (a part of its size) and settles; heartCss: how big it is drawn at far zoom, where creatures are dots (CSS px). arrowPx: how many CSS px one pixel of the arrow is (art.findArrow), the arrow at the field's edge while her finger is down on the name and the one on the card is off the screen; edge: how far in from the field's edge the arrow stays (CSS px). clear: where her card stands over the middle of the field (a 375 px phone), how far above its top the one she finds stands (CSS px).

scrap._note: The Scrapbook (design 14 §4.3, §7 T12) and its cards (his calls, 1 and 2 Oct 2026). shot: the photo cut from the field for a card's back, width and height in canvas pixels (a world pixel each at play size: 8 tiles by 6; kept as a lossless WebP where the browser writes one, about 2.5 KB, else a PNG). card/cardStrip: the postcard's picture (its width) and the strip of Because pictures under it. friendsMax: how many named friends the device keeps (the cards have no cap: every card is kept). glowEveryMs: the header's book never glows more than this often. saveMs: how long writes wait to be batched. ground: the tiles round the place a card's picture shows (columns, rows; 8 px a tile). hours: where a day's dawn, day and dusk end, as a part of the day (night until the next dawn; night falls at rules.nightFrac). across: cards in a row in a section. near: how far below the screen a card is drawn before she scrolls to it, CSS px. madeNear: what a card's row made (a spawn, one turned into another) is there when one of that kind stands this near the moment's place, world px (his cards' review round).

trayCol._note: Tray item columns: at least min px wide, sized so part of the next column always shows (peek of a column), the sign that the tray scrolls.
